description: A node's own AI stack, as committed config: its own chat surface (Open WebUI) standing on its own model server (infra Ollama) and its own vector store (ChromaDB), the declarative slice of adoption item 3 in CLUSTER_INFERENCE_DESIGN.md. Read by peer-node/tests/test_node_ai_stack.py, which fails the build if the committed topology stops being the declared surface the design requires. Cluster fan-out is NOT here: accepting a signed subtask belongs to the task ingress + cluster client (item 5), so nothing in this file can be a vector for delegated inference.

topology.network_mode: host — the surface must reach the node's loopback-only dispatch bridge (127.0.0.1:4096); a bridge-network container cannot reach a loopback-only host listener (host-gateway resolves to the docker0 gateway, not 127.0.0.1)
topology.model_server: the node's infra Ollama, http://127.0.0.1:11434 (never a remote node's overlay address)
topology.vector_store: the node's infra ChromaDB, http://127.0.0.1:18000 (its published port)
topology.why_published: Operator decision (2026-10-10), network choice revised 2026-10-11: the chat surface answers on the node's LAN and overlay addresses. Binding is not the confidentiality control any more — the SPARKNET-FW host firewall restricts 8181/11434/18000 to loopback + LAN + overlay + Docker bridge subnets, so the exposure is a decision with a rule attached, not an omission.

gpu.why: GPU is never required to run, only to change throughput. The committed file declares none; the host deployer adds a device reservation on a node that has one. Docker cannot partition VRAM, so GPU sharing is configured inside the model server, never by slicing containers.

knowledge_bases.vault: the only authored knowledge base; readable only through the grant-checked bridge

open_webui_rag.corpus: structure-only — schema, taxonomy, charters and contracts; never the vault's personal pages
open_webui_rag.why: The operator wants the node's chat surface to know the shape of the fabric without ingesting personal material. The corpus is built from a fixed allow-list and a test asserts no excluded path reaches it, so the vector store never becomes an uncontrolled copy of the vault.

capabilities.why: A node's own prompts are already free and need no capability (COMPUTE_CAPABILITY_DESIGN.md draws the same line: only delegated work is gated). 'cluster-serve' is what a *delegated subtask* would need, and no subtask can reach this stack until item 5; 'sign' belongs to the Master alone and is structurally unobtainable here — the stack mounts no key, no signer socket and no $SPARKNET_STATE_DIR.

webui_surface.declared_not_database_state: Open WebUI's panel is a database click; the surface lives in agent-models.json + this compose env so a redeploy cannot lose it (peer PLAN Step 5 DoD 5).
webui_surface.bridge_route: OPENAI_API_BASE_URLS=http://127.0.0.1:4096/v1 — this node's dispatch bridge, loopback 4096, reached because Open WebUI shares the host network namespace (network_mode: host).
webui_surface.bridge_key: OPENAI_API_KEYS expands a deploy-time signed grant ($SPARKNET_WEBUI_BRIDGE_GRANT); no token is committed and the compose fails loudly while it is unset.
webui_surface.approve_deny: a permission request surfaces as an Approve/Deny card and resolves through POST /session/:id/permissions/:permissionID on the dispatch bridge (peer PLAN Step 5 DoD 2); the decision is recorded in the grant-keyed session.
webui_surface.session_vault_access: POST /session/:id/vault-access toggles per-session 'all vault tools' (mode: all|per-tool). 'all' drops only the presenting grant's own spent nonce so the grant keeps working in that session until it expires; scope, expiry, signature and per-mutation audit are unchanged. Default stays one-shot.
webui_surface.rag: enabled, structure-only corpus, backed by the node's own ChromaDB (peer PLAN Step 5 DoD 4, operator decision 2026-10-10).

conversation_passing.contract: the /session/:id native verbs on the dispatch bridge (peer PLAN Step 6)
conversation_passing.message: POST /session/:id/message accepts an 'agent' and hands the conversation off with history intact (Step 6 DoD 1)
conversation_passing.fork: POST /session/:id/fork at a message index creates a child session carrying the shared prefix; the original stays whole (Step 6 DoD 2)
conversation_passing.children_and_shares: GET /session/:id/children lists the branch; POST/GET/DELETE /session/:id/share[/:id] declare a session-view/session-handoff share in 'open' status (Step 6 DoD 3)
conversation_passing.native_primitives: only native opencode/OpenAI verbs; no custom passing mechanism (Step 6 note)
conversation_passing.regime_not_here: clocks, expiry, cross-node transfer and the kb-*/full share kinds belong to Step 8 and are deliberately absent

masterspike.artifacts: Modelfile + vllm-system-prompt.md, both generated from the one source by scripts/sparknet-masterspike.py (peer PLAN Step 7 DoD 1/2); `make model-verify` fails on divergence or a moved source (DoD 3)
masterspike.selectable: masterspike is in agent-models.json and MODEL_FILTER_LIST (DoD 4)
masterspike.capability_boundary: the model holds no signing capability — the artifacts are text with no key, no signer socket and no state dir, and authority stays Ed25519 in the Master, never a prompt (DoD 4)

signing_boundary.why_structural: A deny rule governs a process that may later ignore it. This stack is declared without the mounts a key or a socket would need, which makes the boundary structural rather than a permission statement.

network_boundary.host_firewall: SPARKNET-FW (iptables DOCKER-USER + INPUT, ip6tables INPUT) on each node
network_boundary.why: Publishing on 0.0.0.0 also publishes on the node's global IPv6. The firewall keeps the fabric fully functional (overlay, LAN, loopback, docker nets, wg1) while blocking direct public-internet reach to those ports.

not_built_yet: This describes the deployed shape; the assertion of a *live* Open WebUI, a running bridge grant and a working firewall is a target-node check. The assertions in test_node_ai_stack.py are read off these files and the compose file, and are therefore only as strong as the files: they prove the declared topology is coherent, not that a real deployment held.
